Th e humble burberry beetle gingerly walks along the branch of a burberry tree to safely hide amongst the leaves. Th is diminutive insect, 
which spends most of the year camouflaged safely among the lower foliage, climbs high as the warm seasons wane. While the natural 
berries of the tree are found shriveled on the branch, the insect brandishes similarly shaped and vibrant orbs to entice migrating 
birds to dart in and consume the false fruit. Nestled within the digestive tracks of the bird, the burberry beetle larvae stay dormant 
throughout the winter and travel great distances within the avian migrations, waiting until the warmth of spring to then emerge in 
their droppings, crawling forth for a new year and new cycle of life.

Encountering As its name implies, the burberry beetle spends 
the majority of its life in a burberry tree and, while fi nding 
the specifi c plant can be simple once a Traveler is within the 
Wealdwoods, discovering the hidden beetle within is a much 
more diffi cult search. Often, the best practice is to roughly 
shake the bush in the hope that the insect will leap out.
A long sail of branching ovipositors rises over 
the insect’s thorax, acting as both a camouflaged 
mimicry of its natural home of tree leaves, and a 
safe method to the eggs far from the core of its body 
from any potentially aggressively hungry birds 
With an incredibly sweet jelly-like 
outer shell, the chorion casing within 
is durable, capable of surviving all but 
the molar teeth of a mammal. The 
egg’s outer shell only dissolves in the 
outdoor elements, after defecation
While the beetle is rather small and 
harmless, the leaves of the burberry 
tree in which its diet entirely subsists on, 
builds up a toxin in its body that can be 
fatal to many predators
